description: FILE STATUS '23' reported by the ACCTFILE keyed read takes the WHEN OTHER arm of the two-arm EVALUATE at app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L403-L410, and this case pins that arm together with the ORDER that reaches it and the eight guard sites that stayed silent on the way (gates G47, G30). UNIT AND INVOCATION: statement.StatementGenerationJobA as a BATCH_JOB, reached at step/Tasklet level with statement.StatementGenerationJobB as its constructor-injected collaborator - no JobLauncher, no job repository and no HTTP anywhere in the path (gate G51). jobParameters is empty because no step of app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL declares a PARM - the only PARM in this estate is INTCALC.jcl's PARM='2022071800' - and STEP040, the step that runs this program, is EXEC PGM=CBSTM03A,COND=(0,NE) at :L79. THREE STATUS-CHECKING CONVENTIONS, AND THEY ARE NEVER UNIFIED. CBSTM03A checks WS-M03B-RC in three textually different ways, and every one of them is a separate contract. CONVENTION A, the opens and the closes: IF WS-M03B-RC = '00' OR '04' / CONTINUE / ELSE DISPLAY 'ERROR <verb> <DD>' / DISPLAY 'RETURN CODE: ' WS-M03B-RC / PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM / END-IF. It appears at NINE sites - the four opens at L736, L771, L789 and L807, the four closes at L862, L879, L895 and L911, and, easily missed, the FIRST TRNXFILE read at L748 inside 8100-TRNXFILE-OPEN, which is a READ that nevertheless uses the OPEN's form and whose literal is 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE'. There is no '10' arm on any of the nine, because end of file is not a meaningful outcome of an open or a close. CONVENTION B, the two SEQUENTIAL reads: a three-arm ordered EVALUATE WS-M03B-RC with WHEN '00' CONTINUE, WHEN '10' and WHEN OTHER - 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT at L353-L362, where '10' moves 'Y' into END-OF-FILE, and 8500-READTRNX-READ at L837-L847, where '00' loops back for the next record and '10' goes to 8599-EXIT. CONVENTION C, the two KEYED reads and the one this case is about: a TWO-arm EVALUATE WS-M03B-RC with WHEN '00' CONTINUE and WHEN OTHER only - 2000-CUSTFILE-GET at L379-L386 and 3000-ACCTFILE-GET at L403-L410. Convention C has no '10' arm at all, so on a keyed read '10' is fatal rather than end of file, which is the complementary fact case14 pins by reporting exactly that status at the CUSTFILE read. Unifying the conventions fails in two opposite directions and both are parity violations: route an open through the read's three-arm EVALUATE and '10' becomes a successful end of file on an open, which it never is; drop the '04' acceptance and a perfectly successful open abends. The '00' OR '04' acceptance is the legacy contract and is preserved exactly as written - not narrowed to '00', not widened, and with nothing emitted on '04' (practice B5). Note also MOVE ZERO TO WS-M03B-RC before the call at all eleven sites that clear it - L349, L375 and L399 for the three reads that clear, L733, L768, L786 and L804 for the four opens, and L859, L876, L892 and L908 for the four closes: the figurative constant ZERO moved into a PIC X(02) receiver fills it with '0' characters, so the field reads '00' before the subroutine answers at all, and a collaborator that answered nothing whatever would be indistinguishable from one that succeeded. The loop read at L832-L835 does not clear it, which is another reason its EVALUATE cannot be interchanged with an open's IF. WHICH ARMS THIS ONE RUN DRIVES, AND WHERE THE REST LIVE. Reaching L403 costs eight earlier status checks and every one of them is an assertion here, made by the ABSENCE of its guard literal from the ordered expectedMessages list rather than by a line in it: Convention A's accept arm on '00' at the TRNXFILE open (L736), at the first TRNXFILE read (L748) and at the XREFFILE, CUSTFILE and ACCTFILE opens (L771, L789, L807); Convention B's '00' arm at the XREFFILE sequential read (L354) and its '10' arm at the loop read (L841), which is what ends the table load with the single seeded row stored and sends control to 8599-EXIT; and Convention C's '00' arm at the CUSTFILE keyed read (L380). Not one 'ERROR OPENING TRNXFILE', 'ERROR READING TRNXFILE', 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE', 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE', 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE', 'ERROR READING XREFFILE' or 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' line appears, and that emptiness is the assertion that each of those eight took its silent branch. The four CLOSE guards are never reached, because the abend happens inside 1000-MAINLINE and 9100 through 9400 run after the loop at L331-L337. The remaining guard arms belong to this program's other cases, one deviation each: case11 reports '04' at the TRNXFILE open and COMPLETES, which is the other half of Convention A's accepted pair; case12 reports '35' at the same open and takes its ELSE; case13 reports '37' at the XREFFILE sequential read and takes Convention B's WHEN OTHER; case14 reports '10' at the CUSTFILE keyed read and takes Convention C's WHEN OTHER, proving the missing '10' arm; case16 reports '38' at the TRNXFILE close and takes Convention A's ELSE after a complete statement has already been written. STATUS PROVENANCE - WHAT THE COLLABORATOR CAN LEGITIMATELY RETURN. CBSTM03B sets LK-M03B-RC by MOVE <ddname>FILE-STATUS TO LK-M03B-RC at L152, L176, L201 and L226, so the value is the raw two-character COBOL FILE STATUS and each of the four DD names has its OWN independent status area. All four files are ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED and all four are opened OPEN INPUT, read-only, at L136, L160, L184 and L209; TRNXFILE (L31-L35) and XREFFILE (L37-L41) are ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL while CUSTFILE (L43-L47) and ACCTFILE (L49-L53) are ACCESS MODE IS RANDOM. '23' is precisely what a RANDOM keyed READ of an indexed file reports when the record key is not present, so the status this case drives sits inside that contract rather than outside it, and it reaches ACCTFILE's status area alone - CUSTFILE's read, performed first, still reports '00'. ORDER PINNED, AND WHY NOTHING IS WRITTEN. WS-FL-DD starts 'TRNXFILE' (L67), so the ALTER/GO TO dispatch at L298-L314 opens TRNXFILE, reads its first record, loads WS-TRNX-TABLE through 8500-READTRNX-READ until '10', then opens XREFFILE, CUSTFILE and ACCTFILE before reaching 1000-MAINLINE. The loop at L317-L329 then performs 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT, and while not at end of file 2000-CUSTFILE-GET, 3000-ACCTFILE-GET, 5000-CREATE-STATEMENT, MOVE 1 TO CR-JMP, MOVE ZERO TO WS-TOTAL-AMT and 4000-TRNXFILE-GET. The customer read at L321 therefore precedes the account read at L322, and the account read precedes every statement write, so this case pins that sequence as firmly as it pins the guard: a translation that read the account before the customer would report '23' with the customer read never attempted, and one that wrote its first statement line before the account read would leave records behind. 5000-CREATE-STATEMENT is never entered, so expectedWrites is empty and that emptiness is a positive assertion, and expectedDatasets nevertheless names both outputs on the WRITES channel with a row count of 0 - the one statement no row expectation can make, and a true one here because OPEN OUTPUT STMT-FILE HTML-FILE at L293 runs in the prologue, before the dispatch, so both datasets exist and are reported having received nothing. The completing shape they were denied is 19 + N STMTFILE records and 64 + 11N HTMLFILE records per statement, which for one transaction is the 20 and 75 that case01 pins; here it is 0 and 0. expectedFinalState is empty and both outputs are pinned at 0 rows on the FINAL_STATE channel as well, because app/jcl/CREASTMT.JCL:L87 and :L92 declare both DISP=(NEW,CATLG,DELETE) and a run that does not reach 9999-GOBACK leaves neither behind - which is the same value for a different reason, and the two channels are therefore asserted separately rather than conflated. SEEDS ARE REAL BYTES. XREFFILE is row 0 of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt verbatim - XREF-CARD-NUM 0500024453765740, XREF-CUST-ID 000000050, XREF-ACCT-ID 00000000050 - and it stays 36 bytes here, exactly as shipped. ParityCase.Normalisation is the sole owner of the 14-space pad up to CVACT03Y's declared 50 and applies it once, at seed time, through the declared CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50, so the fixture is never edited and the pad is never double-applied (gate G16). ACCTFILE and CUSTFILE are acctdata.txt (300 x 50) and custdata.txt (500 x 50) whole. Both keyed reads take their keys from that one xref row - 2000-CUSTFILE-GET with LENGTH OF XREF-CUST-ID = 9 at L374 and 3000-ACCTFILE-GET with LENGTH OF XREF-ACCT-ID = 11 at L398 - so the customer read finds custdata's key 000000050 and succeeds, and the account key 00000000050 exists in acctdata too: the '23' is substituted at the call site rather than manufactured by removing the row, which keeps the seed honest and keeps the case about the guard instead of about a hole in the data. The customer is read through CUSTREC, whose date of birth is CUST-DOB-YYYYMMDD and never CVCUS01Y's CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD; the two copybooks are near-identical and are deliberately kept as separate types so that field name survives (requirement I1). TRNXFILE IS INLINE BECAUSE THERE IS NO TENTH FIXTURE: app/data/ASCII holds exactly nine .txt files and none of them is a statement transaction file, so the single row is composed from app/cpy/COSTM01.CPY at exactly 350 bytes - TRNX-CARD-NUM X(16) plus TRNX-ID X(16) as the 32-byte composite key, then 2 + 4 + 10 + 100 + 11 + 9 + 50 + 50 + 10 + 26 + 26 = 298 plus a trailing FILLER X(20) emitted as spaces = 318 - and its total width is what proves the FILLER was emitted at all (gate G21). Its TRNX-CARD-NUM equals the xref card so the table entry is the one 4000-TRNXFILE-GET would have matched, and rows are ordered ascending by card then id, the order STEP010's SORT FIELDS=(263,16,CH,A,1,16,CH,A) produces; with one row that ordering is trivially satisfied and is stated so a later edit cannot quietly break it. TRNX-AMT '0000000010{' is an 11-byte zoned S9(09)V99 - nine integer digits then two decimals, the last of which is the byte carrying the sign, and '{' is the overpunch for a positive digit zero - so the value is 1.00 and not 0.10: the digit string is 00000000100 and the implied point falls two places from the right, which is exactly the reading that turns case01's '0000001255{' into 125.50. It is never added to anything here, because ADD TRNX-AMT TO WS-TOTAL-AMT at L429 sits inside 4000-TRNXFILE-GET, past the abend; every amount in this migration is a BigDecimal at the declared scale with RoundingMode.DOWN, never HALF_UP, never HALF_EVEN, never double and never float, because the keyword ROUNDED appears zero times in all 28 programs. WIDTHS COME FROM TWO SOURCES EACH. STMTFILE is 80 bytes, from 01 FD-STMTFILE-REC PIC X(80) at L45 and from CREASTMT.JCL LINE 89, DCB=(LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=8000,RECFM=FB), under the STMTFILE DD at line 87. Line 90 of that JCL is genuinely corrupted - verbatim '//         SPACE=(CYL,(1,1),RLSE), 00,RECFM=FB), ATA.VSAM.KSDS', a text-overlay artefact splicing fragments of other lines - and its ' 00,RECFM=FB)' remnant sits directly beneath STMTFILE where it is easily misread as LRECL=100. Line 89 is authoritative, and the JCL is left exactly as it stands: it is the parity oracle, so the hazard is recorded and worked around here rather than corrected there (practices B3, B4). HTMLFILE is 100 bytes, from 01 FD-HTMLFILE-REC PIC X(100) at L47 and from line 94, DCB=(LRECL=100,BLKSIZE=800,RECFM=FB), under the HTMLFILE DD at line 92; that supersedes STEP030's pre-delete LRECL=80,BLKSIZE=3200 at line 69, because the step that creates the dataset wins (risk R-G). Both widths are pinned on both channels here, which is how a dataset expected to be empty still asserts its identity: an empty 80-byte statement file and an empty 100-byte HTML file are not interchangeable just because both are empty (gates G19, G20). MESSAGES AND RETURN CODE. The first nine DISPLAY_LINE expectations are the TIOT walk and nothing else - the job and step line at L270 with TIOTNJOB 'CREASTMT' and TIOTJSTP 'STEP040 ', the 'DD Names from TIOT: ' line at L275, one ' -- valid UCB' line at L279 for each of STEP040's six dataset DDs in JCL declaration order (:L83-:L92; STEPLIB, SYSPRINT and SYSOUT at :L80-:L82 are not data allocations), and the post-loop entry at L290, whose ' -- null  UCB' is byte-different from the in-loop ' --  null UCB' at L281 and where TIOCDDNM X(08) is blank. The last three are the guard's own output, in emission order: DISPLAY 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' at L407, DISPLAY 'RETURN CODE: ' WS-M03B-RC at L408 rendering the 13-character literal followed by the raw two-character status, and DISPLAY 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L922 from 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM, which the guard reaches by PERFORM. expectedReturnCode is 8: L923 is CALL 'CEE3ABD' with no USING clause - the only abend site in the estate that passes neither an ABCODE nor a TIMING - and 8 is the code its nine siblings carry for an assumed failure, mapped onto the step exit status by the shared batch listeners rather than by the job class (gate G35). DETERMINISM. Nothing here is read from a clock. The program composes no timestamp of its own, and the two X(26) spans TRNX-ORIG-TS and TRNX-PROC-TS are seed bytes carrying the fixed 2022-07-18 12:00:00.000000 literal the shipped transaction data uses, never a 'now' (practice B7). Bytes are US-ASCII throughout, matching app/data/ASCII, and never a platform default (practice B8). PROVENANCE: every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of the CBSTM03A and CBSTM03B paragraphs, cross-checked against the COSTM01, CUSTREC, CVACT01Y and CVACT03Y byte layouts, the CREASTMT.JCL DD and DCB contracts and the real ASCII fixtures. It was never captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters that break parsing outright (practice B12, risk R-A). CASE ALLOCATION, RECORDED RATHER THAN RESOLVED BY RENUMBERING: the build prompt for this file described case15 as the success counterpart that reports '04' on all four opens and completes with a return code of 0. In the delivered suite that behaviour is case11 - Scenario.reporting(CallSite.OPEN_TRNXFILE, FileStatus.RECORD_LENGTH_CONFLICT), a run that completes - while CBSTM03AParityTest.scenario(String) pairs case15 with CallSite.READ_ACCTFILE and '23'; the frozen ParityCase contract carries no member by which a batch case could inject a status at all, and a Scenario names exactly one call site, so an injection at four separate opens is not expressible. Rather than renumber a sibling's completed case or leave 3000-ACCTFILE-GET's WHEN OTHER without a case and lose that arm from gate G47, the conflict is documented here (practice B4) and the substance is delivered in place: the '00' OR '04' acceptance is preserved verbatim and asserted on its '00' side by this case at all five Convention A sites it reaches, and on its '04' side by case11. HOW THE ENVIRONMENT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA: the substituted file status below used to be chosen by a Java switch over this file's case identifier, which meant this file gave no indication of the environment it ran in, renumbering it would have silently moved that environment to a different run, and a case file added without a matching Java arm would have thrown or fallen into an arm asserting something it had not asked for. The environment is an INPUT, so it is declared here beside the seed that is also an input, under unitStimulus. unitStimulus names READ-ACCTFILE reporting FILE STATUS '23' at the keyed read of app/cbl/CBSTM03A.CBL:L401. The guard at L403 has only a WHEN '00' and a WHEN OTHER, so a record-not-found on the account master is fatal here rather than a condition the program recovers from - which is behaviour, not a defect, and is preserved as such (gates G47, G35).
